finalists.label: Histoplasmosis
finalists.why: Strong evidence from urine histoplasma antigen, laryngeal biopsy, and fungal culture.

finalists.label: Disseminated histoplasmosis
finalists.why: Similar evidence to Histoplasmosis, but considered in the context of immunodeficiency.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of specific findings like rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain and the growth of Histoplasma capsulatum in fungal culture, along with a positive urine histoplasma antigen, decisively support Histoplasmosis over its disseminated form, given the lack of systemic symptoms.

support_spans: Urine histoplasma antigen: positive at 0.3 ng/mL
Laryngeal biopsy revealed rare hyphae and yeast forms on Grocott methenamine silver stain with no evidence of malignancy or granulomas
Fungal culture grew Histoplasma capsulatum, identified by typical tuberculate microconidia
contradict_spans: no systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, myalgias) or pulmonary symptoms

support_spans: medical history significant for idiopathic CD4 lymphocytopenia (ICL) originally diagnosed in 2015
with an annual CD4 cell count ranging between 14 and 18 cells/µL
Laryngeal cultures initially grew Streptococcus mitis, Streptococcus salivarius, Rothia mucilaginosus, Neisseria flavescens/subflava, and Candida albicans
